researched_by: local press reporting of the council's April 2026 proposals
policy_summary:
The 'Motorhome Aire' scheme: six short-stay overnight sites across the county, deliberately sited at what the council calls known hot-spots for unauthorised overnight stays. Explicitly modelled on French aires - low-cost stopping places with limited facilities.

The council's own framing is worth quoting: in Denbighshire there is no legal right to sleep overnight in a vehicle. The aires exist to give the displaced traffic somewhere legitimate, not to grant a right that did not exist.

Marine Drive in Rhyl drew the strongest local opposition of the six.
notes: Provision-led rather than enforcement-led, and unusually well documented - all six locations are named down to which part of each car park. Compare Conwy next door, which prohibits overnight camping everywhere.
open_questions: Are any of the six actually open? Reported as progressing in April 2026.
Price and maximum stay - 'short stay' is all that has been said.
What instrument covers them, and what covers the Marine Drive restriction?
Did the Marine Drive opposition change anything?

sites.name: Quay Street, Rhyl
sites.notes: Corner section of a currently closed car park, with the rest allocated to coach parking. Part of the six-site Motorhome Aire scheme, reported as progressing April 2026. Price and terms not yet published.

sites.name: Marine Drive (East Parade), Rhyl
sites.notes: Small area close to the Pavilion. The most contested of the six - residents objected strongly. Part of the six-site Motorhome Aire scheme, reported as progressing April 2026. Price and terms not yet published.

sites.name: Overnight sleeping in a vehicle, county-wide
sites.notes: Council position as reported: there is no legal right to sleep overnight in a vehicle in Denbighshire. The aires are the exception being created, not a relaxation of the rule.
